touches.text: Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Owns no state of its own. May use any library, other tools included. Lives in cairn/tools/ (17). Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/. WHY: the rule keeps encapsulation useful inside our world, so the system stays within the complexity CC can manage. Forbidding libraries would forbid opening files. -amm
ground_loop (machine): the heartbeat
INTENTION:
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.

Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead.

A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, because even the Laws rest finally on the core principles. Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).
TOOLS: base, cgroup; the Gmail/Calendar code and CC's browser (ccfox), with their data under ~/.cairn/devices/cc/0/tools/<tool>/ (1.3.1).
import_sieve: one parse of every .py into an import graph; what reaches what. WHY: enforces "only the proxy reaches the host/database" and RULE 1 by physics. USERS: CodeMother, the inference proxy.

The RULE 1 check is a path check: code inside device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo (anything not under cairn.devices.bar), except a tool foo publishes (cairn.devices.foo.tools.<x>, its charter saying published_by_device). Inside one device there is one owner, so nothing is checked there. A charter's public_interface describes what the component offers (modules, functions, bus verbs, commands); the check does not read it. WHY: a path check is the simplest thing the code can test.

RULE 1, ENCAPSULATION: every component talks to every other only through that component's public interface: a device's is the bus plus any client tool it publishes; a machine's or tool's is what its entry declares. Nothing outside a device reaches into its code, skills included. A ticket builds inside its own component, and its proofs measure only that component. WHY: it limits a change to the component that made it.
Physics: the encapsulation_holds sieve in build_inspector, a device-path check. Code in device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo except a tool foo publishes. Inside one device nothing is checked.
It launches each device's cairn/devices/<device>/groundloop/pulse.py, each as its own process (5.8.3.4).
tester
build_inspector
It outputs only its findings. It certifies nothing, records no crossing, and posts nothing; the gate consumes its findings.

A rule not yet enforced is made into a ticket now, never left floating as prose. So ticket f5dbfddea8c6 makes the rewrites it proposed at the remaining sites (the press office, PROOF.md). Where a site names a rule whose physics is not built, it names that rule's real ticket id, cast now if none exists; the word "ticket" with no id behind it does not count. - CC

The only way to the inference host; anything that goes around it is an error. WHY: its two points are to find the cheapest model powerful enough for each request, and to train the graph trees on the results.
cgroup: reads which cgroup a process lives in. WHY: 10.3.2. USERS: CC, artifact.

Machine: tools plus the glue that holds them together. Has an owner. Anything that calls a machine or device, or owns state it must gate, is a machine. Lives inside its device (cairn/devices/<device>/machines/<machine>/), or in cairn/machines/ when several devices hold one (16).
Tools and machines are peers in the tree; the rung is complexity, not rank.

Commit: the proofs of the component the ticket changed, since RULE 1 bounds a change to its component. Passing them puts the component in service, yellow: proven where it changed, not yet measured against what depends on it. In service needs only the best we can do now: 80% trust.
